name: Old town, Saumur
name_zh: 索米尔 · 老城
note_en: Old Grandet, the most famous miser in all of literature, lives in this Loire Valley town. Eugénie Grandet opens with Balzac walking us up the steep street to the château, past old timber houses with grotesque faces carved into their beams. The Grandet house itself is made up, but the street and the old town below the château are still here
note: 文学史上最有名的吝啬鬼老葛朗台就住在这座卢瓦尔河小城。《欧也妮·葛朗台》开篇，巴尔扎克带读者走上从城里通向城堡的陡街，看两旁雕着怪脸的木梁老屋。葛朗台家是虚构的，但那条街和城堡下的老城都还在

name: Upper and lower towns, Angoulême
name_zh: 昂古莱姆 · 上城与下城
note_en: Lost Illusions starts here. Lucien, a young poet, is born in L'Houmeau, the merchants' quarter at the bottom of the hill, and dreams of being welcomed into the aristocratic salons up in the old town on top. Balzac turned the town's upper and lower halves into the upper and lower classes of French society. He stayed in Angoulême himself with friends
note: 《幻灭》的起点。诗人吕西安生在山下商人聚居的乌莫，一心想挤进山顶上城的贵族沙龙，最后去了巴黎。巴尔扎克把一座城的上下两层写成了社会的上下两层。他本人在这里的朋友家住过

name: La Mare au Diable, Mers-sur-Indre
name_zh: 安德尔河畔梅尔 · 魔沼
note_en: The pool in the Chanteloube woods is associated with Sand’s story; its present size and surroundings should not be treated as an exact reconstruction of the novel
note: 尚特卢布林中的池塘与乔治·桑的小说相联系；现今水面大小及周边环境不等于书中场景的精确复原
prototype_of: 《魔沼》里那片池塘和森林：年轻的鳏夫热尔曼和牧羊女小玛丽在秋夜的大雾里迷路，在魔沼边过了一夜，两人的心意也在这一夜里明白。乔治·桑把她诺昂周围的贝里乡村写成了一系列田园小说，这片林间池塘至今可以走到
prototype_of_en: These woods and this pond are the setting of The Devil's Pool. Germain, a young widower, and Marie, a shepherd girl, get lost in the fog one autumn night and spend it by the pond, and by morning they understand how they feel about each other. George Sand set a whole series of country novels in the Berry region around her home at Nohant, and you can still walk out to the pond

name: Illiers-Combray
name_zh: 伊利耶-贡布雷 · 小城
note_en: Illiers helped inspire the fictional Combray; the marker represents the town, while Proust combines remembered and invented geography
note: 伊利耶是虚构贡布雷的灵感来源之一；标记代表城镇，普鲁斯特将记忆与想象中的地理融合
prototype_of: 《追忆似水年华》贡布雷的原型：普鲁斯特童年在姑妈家过复活节假期的小城。1971 年普鲁斯特百年诞辰时，伊利耶正式改名伊利耶-贡布雷，这是法国唯一一座以小说里的地名改名的城镇
prototype_of_en: Illiers is the real Combray from In Search of Lost Time. As a boy, Proust spent his Easter holidays here with his aunt. In 1971, to mark the hundredth anniversary of his birth, the town officially renamed itself Illiers-Combray. It's the only town in France to take its name from a place in a novel

name: Saint-Jacques Church, Illiers-Combray
name_zh: 伊利耶-贡布雷 · 圣雅克教堂
note_en: One model for the composite Saint-Hilaire church of Combray; the fictional porch and interior do not reproduce this building feature for feature
note: 贡布雷圣伊莱尔教堂的多个原型之一；小说中的门廊与内部陈设并非这座建筑的逐项复制
prototype_of: 贡布雷圣伊莱尔教堂的原型之一：小说里，从十法里外远看贡布雷，整座城就只是这座教堂的钟楼。普鲁斯特把伊利耶这座圣雅克教堂和别处的教堂糅在一起，写成了书里最有名的教堂
prototype_of_en: This church is one of the models for Saint-Hilaire in Combray. In the novel, when you see Combray from far away, the whole town seems to be nothing but this church's steeple. Proust blended Saint-Jacques with a few other churches to create the most famous church in his book

name: Citadel of Besançon
name_zh: 贝桑松 · 城堡
note_en: In The Red and the Black, Julien leaves his small hometown for the seminary in Besançon. The first thing he sees is the citadel up on the hill, and what he really wants is to be a soldier. The fortress, built by Vauban, is now a World Heritage Site. Besançon is also where Victor Hugo was born, in 1802
note: 《红与黑》里于连离开小城维里埃，来到贝桑松进神学院，远远先看见山上的城堡，心里想的却是当兵。这座沃邦修建的城堡现为世界遗产。贝桑松也是雨果 1802 年出生的地方

name: Rouen
name_zh: 鲁昂 · 城市与河流
note_en: Rouen is Flaubert's hometown, and the big city Emma Bovary dreams about. She meets Léon at the cathedral, and then the two of them spend an entire afternoon riding around town in a cab with the blinds pulled down. That scene was one of the reasons the novel was put on trial for obscenity in 1857. The hospital where Flaubert was born is now a museum about him and the history of medicine
note: 福楼拜的故乡，也是《包法利夫人》里爱玛向往的“大城市”。她和莱昂在大教堂约会，随后坐进一辆拉上窗帘的马车在城里兜了一下午——这一幕让小说 1857 年被告上法庭。福楼拜出生的市立医院现为福楼拜与医学史博物馆

name: Ry, associated with Yonville
name_zh: 里村 · 永镇原型
note_en: Ry is traditionally associated with Yonville, but this identification is debated and the fictional town is a composite; the Rieule is not the real river’s name
note: 里村传统上被视为永镇原型，但这一认定有争议，虚构城镇融合了多处素材；里厄勒并非当地真实河流的名称
prototype_of: 《包法利夫人》永镇的原型（传统说法，有争议）：据说里村一位乡村医生的妻子德尔菲娜·德拉马尔的故事启发了福楼拜，她 1848 年年纪轻轻就死了。小村一直以“爱玛的村子”自居，照片里这座雕花木门廊是村里最老的建筑之一
prototype_of_en: Ry has long been called the real Yonville from Madame Bovary, though not everyone agrees. The story goes that Flaubert was inspired by Delphine Delamare, the wife of a country doctor here, who died young in 1848. The village has proudly called itself Emma's village ever since. The carved wooden porch in the photo is one of the oldest things in town

name: Anzin mining district
name_zh: 昂赞 · 矿区原型
note_en: Zola researched the Anzin miners in 1884; the marker represents this source region for Montsou and its mining settlements, not an exact fictional pit or road
note: 左拉于1884年实地考察昂赞矿工；标记代表蒙苏及矿工村的素材来源地区，不指认某口虚构矿井或某段道路
prototype_of: 《萌芽》里蒙苏煤矿和矿工村的原型：1884 年昂赞矿工大罢工期间，左拉亲自来到这里，下到矿井、走进工人的家，记了几百页笔记。北部-加来海峡采矿盆地 2012 年列为世界遗产，附近的勒瓦尔德采矿历史中心可以下矿参观
prototype_of_en: The coal mine and miners' village in Germinal are based on this area. In 1884, during a huge miners' strike at Anzin, Zola came here himself. He went down into the pits, visited workers in their homes, and filled hundreds of pages with notes. The Nord-Pas-de-Calais mining basin became a World Heritage Site in 2012, and the mining museum at nearby Lewarde takes visitors underground

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 圣母院
note_en: Hugo wrote The Hunchback of Notre-Dame partly to save the cathedral. In 1831 it was crumbling and nobody seemed to care. The novel was such a success that in 1844 the government hired the architect Viollet-le-Duc to restore it, and he added the spire and the famous chimeras. After the fire of 2019, Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024
note: 雨果写《巴黎圣母院》，一半是为了救这座教堂：1831 年小说出版时，大教堂年久失修，几乎没人在意。小说轰动之后，政府才在 1844 年请维奥莱-勒-杜克大修，尖塔和那些著名的怪兽石雕都是那时加的。2019 年大火后，圣母院于 2024 年 12 月重新开放

name: Former Place de Grève, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 原格雷沃广场
note_en: In The Hunchback of Notre-Dame, this is the square where Quasimodo is whipped in public and where Esmeralda is taken to be hanged. For centuries it was Paris's place of execution. It was also where workers came to wait for jobs, which is where the French expression for going on strike, faire grève, comes from. Today it's the square in front of City Hall
note: 《巴黎圣母院》里卡西莫多受鞭刑、爱斯梅拉达被送上绞架的广场，几百年来是巴黎的刑场。失业工人也常聚在这里等活干，法语“罢工”（faire grève）一词就是从这里来的。今天是市政厅广场

name: Digne-les-Bains
name_zh: 迪涅 · 城镇
note_en: Les Misérables begins in Digne. Just out of prison and turned away everywhere, Jean Valjean is taken in by Bishop Myriel. That night he steals the bishop's silver. When the police drag him back, the bishop tells them it was a gift, and then hands him the silver candlesticks too. That moment changes Valjean's life. The bishop was based on a real bishop of Digne, Monseigneur de Miollis
note: 《悲惨世界》开始的地方。冉阿让出狱后走投无路，只有迪涅的米里哀主教收留了他；他偷走银器被抓回，主教却说那是送他的，还把一对银烛台也给了他——这一夜改变了他的一生。主教的原型是真实的迪涅主教米奥利斯

name: Ajaccio and its gulf
name_zh: 阿雅克肖 · 城市与海湾
note_en: Colomba opens as a ship sails into the Bay of Ajaccio, at the start of a story about a Corsican blood feud. Mérimée toured Corsica in 1839 as France's inspector of historic monuments and came home with this novel. Ajaccio is also where Napoleon was born
note: 《科隆巴》里一家人从海上驶进阿雅克肖湾，开始一个科西嘉复仇的故事。梅里美 1839 年以历史古迹总监的身份考察科西嘉，带回了这部小说。阿雅克肖也是拿破仑的出生地

name: Trouville-sur-Mer beach
name_zh: 特鲁维尔 · 海滩
note_en: In the 1800s, Trouville was the most fashionable beach in Normandy. In Pierre and Jean, Pierre arrives by boat and sees the beach covered in colorful umbrellas, like a flower garden. Years earlier, in 1836, a fourteen-year-old Flaubert met Madame Schlésinger on this beach. He loved her for the rest of his life and put that love into Sentimental Education
note: 十九世纪最时髦的诺曼底海滩。《皮埃尔与让》里皮埃尔坐船来到这里，远看满滩彩色阳伞像一座花园。更早的 1836 年，十四岁的福楼拜在这片海滩上遇见施莱辛格夫人，从此爱了她一辈子，后来写进了《情感教育》

name: Cap de la Hève lighthouse site
name_zh: 圣阿德雷斯 · 拉埃沃角灯塔旧址
note_en: In Pierre and Jean, Pierre walks along the harbor at night, troubled, and watches the twin electric lighthouses on Cap de la Hève sweep the sea like a pair of one-eyed giants. Those twin towers are gone now, but a lighthouse still stands on the cliff nearby
note: 《皮埃尔与让》里，心事重重的皮埃尔夜里在勒阿弗尔港边散步，看拉埃沃角上那对电灯灯塔像两个独眼巨人照着海面。那对双塔已经不在，今天的灯塔立在原处附近的悬崖上
coord_checked: Cap de la Hève lighthouse site — https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phare_de_la_H%C3%A8ve

name: Le Havre harbour
name_zh: 勒阿弗尔 · 港湾
note_en: Pierre and Jean takes place in Le Havre. An unexpected inheritance drives a wedge between two brothers, and as Pierre wanders among the lights of the port, he slowly figures out his mother's secret. Maupassant grew up nearby in Étretat and wrote about this port city as if it were his own backyard
note: 《皮埃尔与让》的故事发生在勒阿弗尔：一笔意外的遗产让兄弟俩反目，哥哥皮埃尔在港口的灯火之间一点点猜出了母亲的秘密。莫泊桑在附近的埃特雷塔长大，把这座港城写得像自己家门口

name: Saint-Malo and the Sillon
name_zh: 圣马洛 · 城墙与西永堤道
note_en: Chateaubriand was born in this walled seaside town in 1768, and he came back to it in death. He's buried on the tiny island of Grand Bé, just offshore, in a grave with no name, only a cross facing the sea. You can walk out to it only at low tide. When the tide comes in, the island is cut off
note: 夏多布里昂 1768 年生在这座海上城，死后也回到了这里：他葬在城外的大贝岛上，墓上没有名字，只有一个十字架面朝大海。这座小岛只有退潮时才能走过去，潮水一涨就成了孤岛

name: Château de Combourg
name_zh: 贡堡 · 城堡
note_en: Chateaubriand spent his teenage years in this gloomy castle, and some of the most famous chapters of his Memoirs from Beyond the Grave are set here. His father paced the great hall at night, and young François slept alone in a tower that was said to be haunted by an old lord with a wooden leg and a black cat. The castle still belongs to the family and opens to visitors in summer
note: 夏多布里昂在这座阴森的城堡里度过少年时代，《墓畔回忆录》里最有名的几章写的就是这里：父亲夜里在大厅踱步，他独自睡在塔楼上，传说那里有个装木腿的老领主带着一只黑猫出没。城堡至今是家族产业，夏季开放参观

name: Plancoët
name_zh: 普朗科埃 · 外祖母家所在小镇
note_en: As a baby, Chateaubriand was sent to live with a nurse in Plancoët, and as a boy he often came back to his grandmother's house here. Its garden ran down in terraces to a spring surrounded by willows. Those images became some of the gentlest memories in his Memoirs
note: 夏多布里昂出生后被送到普朗科埃奶妈家，童年常回这里的外祖母家：花园一级级通向谷底，泉边绕着柳树。这些画面后来成了《墓畔回忆录》里最温柔的回忆

name: Montreuil-sur-Mer
name_zh: 蒙特勒伊滨海 · 小城
note_en: This is the town where Jean Valjean, living under the name Monsieur Madeleine, builds a business, gets rich, and becomes mayor. It's also where Fantine's story plays out. Hugo passed through in 1837 and later set this part of the novel here. Every summer the town puts on a huge outdoor production of Les Misérables beneath its old walls
note: 冉阿让改名马德兰先生、办厂致富并当上市长的小城，芳汀的故事也发生在这里。雨果 1837 年路过这里，后来把小说的这一部分设在此地。如今小城每年夏天在城墙下演出《悲惨世界》大型实景剧

name: Loire quays, Nantes
name_zh: 南特 · 卢瓦尔河码头
note_en: In A Little Tour in France, Henry James writes about the gray light along the river in this port city at the mouth of the Loire. Nantes is also where Jules Verne was born, in 1828. As a boy he watched ships leave the docks for faraway places, and he grew up to write Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. The city has a museum dedicated to him
note: 卢瓦尔河口的港城，亨利·詹姆斯在《法国小游记》里写它河岸的灰色光线。这里也是凡尔纳 1828 年出生的地方，他小时候看着码头上的船出海，后来写出了《海底两万里》；城里有凡尔纳博物馆

name: Garonne quays, Bordeaux
name_zh: 波尔多 · 加龙河码头
note_en: Henry James found Bordeaux a grand and handsome merchant city. Its long row of eighteenth-century stone buildings along the Garonne is still the city's best face, and it's now a World Heritage Site. More than four hundred years ago, Montaigne, the author of the Essays, served two terms as mayor here
note: 亨利·詹姆斯笔下气派的商业城市，加龙河边一整排十八世纪的石砌立面至今还是城市的门面，现为世界遗产。四百多年前，写《随笔集》的蒙田当过两任波尔多市长

name: Cité de Carcassonne
name_zh: 卡尔卡松 · 城塞
note_en: Carcassonne is the most complete medieval walled city in Europe, with more than fifty towers along its double walls. Much of what you see today comes from a major restoration in the 1800s by the architect Viollet-le-Duc. When Henry James visited in 1882, the work was still going on, and he said the place looked like a castle out of a Gustave Doré illustration
note: 欧洲最完整的中世纪城塞，双重城墙上有五十多座塔楼。它能有今天的样子，靠的是十九世纪维奥莱-勒-杜克的大修复。亨利·詹姆斯 1882 年来时修复正在进行，他在书里说它像古斯塔夫·多雷画里的城堡

name: Palais des Papes, Avignon
name_zh: 阿维尼翁 · 教皇宫
note_en: The popes lived in Avignon in the fourteenth century, and this was the largest Gothic palace in Europe. In 1327, in a church in this city, the poet Petrarch first laid eyes on Laura, and he spent the rest of his life writing sonnets to her. When Henry James came through, the palace was being used as army barracks. Just outside is the broken bridge from the famous children's song
note: 十四世纪教皇驻在阿维尼翁，这座宫殿是当时欧洲最大的哥特式宫殿。1327 年，彼特拉克在这座城里的圣克莱尔教堂第一次见到劳拉，为她写了一辈子十四行诗。亨利·詹姆斯来时宫殿还是兵营，宫外就是那座唱进童谣的断桥

name: Palace of the Dukes of Burgundy, Dijon
name_zh: 第戎 · 勃艮第公爵宫
note_en: The Dukes of Burgundy were once richer than the kings of France, and this palace was their seat of power. By the time Henry James came, it had become the town hall, and he spent some time admiring the half-moon-shaped square in front of it. Today it houses Dijon's art museum, where you can see the dukes' elaborate tombs
note: 勃艮第公爵曾是比法国国王还富有的诸侯，这座宫殿是他们的权力中心。亨利·詹姆斯来时它已改作市政厅，他细看了宫前那座半圆形广场。如今宫里是第戎美术馆，公爵们华丽的陵墓就陈列在这里
coord_checked: Palace of the Dukes of Burgundy, Dijon — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_the_Dukes_of_Burgundy

name: Saint-Julien Cathedral, Le Mans
name_zh: 勒芒 · 圣朱利安大教堂
note_en: As soon as Henry James arrived in Le Mans, he headed straight for the cathedral and stood staring up at its soaring choir and its tiers of flying buttresses. The buttresses of Saint-Julien are some of the most spectacular in France, and the building itself, half Romanesque and half Gothic, is like a history of architecture in stone
note: 亨利·詹姆斯一到勒芒就直奔大教堂，仰看它高耸的唱诗堂和层层叠叠的飞扶壁。圣朱利安大教堂的飞扶壁是法国最壮观的之一，一半罗马式、一半哥特式的教堂本身就是一部建筑史

name: Roman amphitheatre, Nîmes
name_zh: 尼姆 · 罗马竞技场
note_en: This Roman arena is two thousand years old and is still used for bullfights and concerts. Henry James spent an hour sitting in it alone on a bright Sunday morning, and in A Little Tour in France he describes the arena's great oval against the sky
note: 两千年前的罗马竞技场，至今还在用来斗牛和办音乐会。亨利·詹姆斯在一个晴朗的星期天早晨独自坐在看台上待了一个小时，《法国小游记》写下了他看到的那条椭圆形天际线

name: Le Monastier-sur-Gazeille
name_zh: 加泽耶河畔勒莫纳斯捷 · 集市小镇
note_en: In September 1878, Robert Louis Stevenson bought a donkey named Modestine in this market town for sixty-five francs and a glass of brandy. He then spent twelve days walking with her across the Cévennes mountains, a trip that became Travels with a Donkey. The Stevenson Trail, a long-distance hiking path, starts right here, and plenty of hikers still rent a donkey for the journey
note: 1878 年 9 月，史蒂文森在这个集市小镇花 65 法郎和一杯白兰地买下母驴莫黛斯婷，牵着它走了十二天，翻越塞文山脉，写成《骑驴漫游记》。今天的“史蒂文森小路”（GR70 徒步道）就从这里出发，不少人还会租一头驴同行

name: Florac
name_zh: 弗洛拉克 · 小城
note_en: Stevenson stopped in Florac on his way across the Cévennes. This was the land of the Camisards, Protestant rebels who rose up in the early 1700s. He describes the castle, the walk lined with plane trees, and the mountain spring, as well as how the locals still remembered those religious wars
note: 史蒂文森穿过塞文山脉时的歇脚小城，这一带是十八世纪初新教徒“卡米扎尔”起义的地方。他在书里写了城堡、悬铃木林荫道和山泉，也写了当地人对那段宗教战争的记忆

name: Saint-Jean-du-Gard
name_zh: 圣让迪加尔 · 小镇
note_en: Travels with a Donkey ends here. Stevenson sold Modestine in Saint-Jean-du-Gard, and only once he was riding away in the coach did he realize how much he'd miss her. On the last page of the book he admits he cried. This is still the end of the Stevenson Trail, and people in town still tell the story
note: 《骑驴漫游记》的终点。史蒂文森在这里卖掉了莫黛斯婷，坐上马车离开时才发现自己舍不得它，在书的最后为它哭了一场。这是史蒂文森小路的终点，镇上的人还会跟你讲这个故事

name: Masevaux
name_zh: 马斯沃 · 圣马丁教堂所在小城
note_en: Alsace was handed over to Germany in 1871. At the start of the First World War, French troops took back these southern valleys, and they were the only part of Alsace that France held for the entire war. On All Saints' Day in 1918, the American writer Edith O'Shaughnessy joined the crowds and soldiers at Masevaux's pink sandstone church and wrote down what she saw
note: 阿尔萨斯 1871 年被割给德国，一战一开始法军就收回了这片南部河谷，这里成了整场战争中唯一在法国手里的阿尔萨斯土地。1918 年诸圣节，美国作家奥肖内西随人群和士兵来到马斯沃的玫瑰色砂岩教堂，写下战时阿尔萨斯的样子

name: Saint-Thiébaut collegiate church, Thann
name_zh: 坦恩 · 圣蒂埃博教堂
note_en: Thann's church is one of the most beautiful Gothic buildings in Alsace, with a spire that looks like lace carved from stone. During the First World War, Thann was one of the Alsatian towns France managed to hold, and when O'Shaughnessy came in 1918, the church was still protected by wooden planks and sandbags
note: 阿尔萨斯最精美的哥特式教堂之一，钟楼的尖顶像石头织成的花边。一战时坦恩是法军守住的阿尔萨斯小城，奥肖内西 1918 年来时，教堂里还垒着护墙的木板和沙袋

name: Saint-Amarin
name_zh: 圣阿马兰 · 中央街道
note_en: When O'Shaughnessy arrived in Saint-Amarin in 1918, a battalion of soldiers from Marseille was marching down the main street in their sky-blue uniforms. She said the whole street looked like a pale blue ribbon. It's a snapshot of a French town in the last weeks of the war
note: 1918 年奥肖内西进圣阿马兰时，一营穿天蓝色军装的马赛士兵正从中央街道走过，她说整条街像一条淡蓝色缎带。这是战争最后几个星期里一个法国收复区小镇的样子

name: Maison de Victor Hugo, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 雨果故居
note_en: Victor Hugo lived on the second floor of 6 Place des Vosges from 1832 to 1848, when he was at the height of his fame, and he started writing Les Misérables here. The apartment is now a free museum. Its most striking room is the Chinese Salon, which Hugo designed himself for his lover, Juliette Drouet, while he was in exile on Guernsey. It was later moved here piece by piece
note: 雨果 1832 至 1848 年住在孚日广场 6 号的二楼，正是他声名最盛的年代，《悲惨世界》也是在这里动笔的。故居现为免费开放的博物馆，最特别的是那间“中国厅”：雨果流亡根西岛时亲手为情人朱丽叶设计的，后来整个搬到了这里

name: Château de Saché, Balzac Museum
name_zh: 萨谢 · 巴尔扎克博物馆
note_en: Whenever Balzac was drowning in debt in Paris, he would escape to a friend's château in Saché to write. He worked from midnight until noon, fueled by endless cups of strong coffee. He wrote part of Father Goriot here, as well as The Lily of the Valley, which is set in the Indre Valley right below the château. His bedroom has been kept just as it was
note: 巴黎欠下一屁股债的巴尔扎克，常躲到朋友在萨谢的城堡里来写作，每天喝着浓咖啡从半夜写到中午。《高老头》的一部分和《幽谷百合》都在这里写成，后者的故事就发生在城堡下的安德尔河谷。他住过的房间保留至今

name: House of George Sand, Nohant
name_zh: 诺昂 · 乔治·桑故居
note_en: George Sand spent most of her life at Nohant, and her house was one of the liveliest artistic gathering places in nineteenth-century France. Chopin spent seven summers here and wrote many of his greatest pieces, and Liszt, Delacroix, Balzac, and Flaubert all came to stay. The house still has her dining table, her study, and the puppet theater her son built
note: 乔治·桑在诺昂度过了大半生，这里是十九世纪法国最热闹的文艺沙龙之一：肖邦在这里度过七个夏天、写下许多名作，李斯特、德拉克洛瓦、巴尔扎克、福楼拜都来做过客。故居保留着她的餐桌、书房和她儿子做的木偶剧场

name: Stendhal Museum, Appartement Gagnon, Grenoble
name_zh: 格勒诺布尔 · 司汤达博物馆
note_en: Stendhal couldn't stand his hometown of Grenoble. The one place he was happy as a child was here, in the apartment of his grandfather, Dr. Gagnon, who read with him, taught him about plants, and gave him his love of books. Stendhal wrote about those years in his autobiography, The Life of Henry Brulard. The apartment is now a Stendhal museum
note: 司汤达一辈子讨厌家乡格勒诺布尔，唯一的温暖来自外祖父加尼翁医生的这套公寓：外祖父带他读书、认植物，教会他热爱文学。他在自传《亨利·布吕拉尔的一生》里写了这段童年，这里现为司汤达博物馆

name: Maison de Tante Léonie, Illiers-Combray
name_zh: 伊利耶-贡布雷 · 莱奥妮姑妈之家
note_en: This is the house where the madeleine comes from. Proust spent his childhood holidays here with his aunt, and in the novel it's Aunt Léonie who dips the little cake into her lime-blossom tea and gives him a taste. The house is now the Proust museum, with Léonie's bedroom upstairs and the kitchen and garden downstairs arranged just as they are in the book
note: 小玛德莱娜蛋糕的故事就是从这座房子里来的：普鲁斯特童年在姑妈家度假，小说里莱奥妮姑妈把蛋糕泡进椴花茶递给他。房子现为普鲁斯特博物馆，楼上莱奥妮姑妈的卧室、楼下的厨房和花园都照小说布置

name: Pavillon Flaubert, Croisset
name_zh: 康特勒 · 克鲁瓦塞福楼拜亭
note_en: Flaubert lived at Croisset, on the banks of the Seine, for more than thirty years, and he spent almost five of them writing Madame Bovary. He tested every sentence by shouting it out loud, a habit he called his 'gueuloir,' or yelling room. After he died, the house was torn down to make way for a distillery. Only this small garden pavilion survived, and it holds some of his belongings
note: 福楼拜在塞纳河边的克鲁瓦塞住了三十多年，《包法利夫人》前后写了将近五年，每写完一句都要大声吼出来听听顺不顺，他管这叫“吼叫”（gueuloir）。他死后主宅被拆，盖了酿酒厂，只剩下花园尽头这座小亭，里面陈列着他的一些遗物

name: Rue Tournefort (former Rue Neuve-Sainte-Geneviève), Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 图尔讷福街（原新圣热纳维埃芙街）
note_en: Balzac put the shabby Maison Vauquer of Father Goriot on this street, then called Rue Neuve-Sainte-Geneviève, wedged between the Latin Quarter and the poor Faubourg Saint-Marceau; the retired noodle-maker Goriot, the convict Vautrin and young Rastignac up from the provinces all lodge here. The boarding house is invented, but the street is real: today's Rue Tournefort, just behind the Panthéon and Rue Mouffetard, and still as quiet as Balzac made it
note: 巴尔扎克把《高老头》里那座寒酸的伏盖公寓放在这条街上，当年叫新圣热纳维埃芙街，夹在拉丁区和贫穷的圣马塞尔区之间：退休面条商高老头、苦役犯伏脱冷和外省青年拉斯蒂涅都住在这里。公寓是虚构的，街道还在，今天叫图尔讷福街，就在穆夫塔尔街和先贤祠背后，安静得像巴尔扎克写的那样

name: Père Lachaise Cemetery, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 拉雪兹神父公墓
note_en: Father Goriot ends here: having buried the old man, Rastignac stands alone on the heights of Père Lachaise, looks down at Paris as its lights come on along the Seine, and says 'It's between you and me now!', a line that has stood for ambition ever since. Balzac himself is buried here, along with Molière, Chopin, Proust and Oscar Wilde, so pick up a map at the gate and take your time
note: 《高老头》的结尾：拉斯蒂涅送走了高老头，独自站在拉雪兹神父公墓的高处，望着塞纳河两岸灯火初上的巴黎，说出那句“现在咱们俩来拼一拼吧！”，从此成了野心家的代名词。巴尔扎克自己也葬在这里，此外还有莫里哀、肖邦、普鲁斯特和王尔德，进门拿一张地图慢慢找

name: Rue de la Michodière, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 米绍迪耶尔街
note_en: Zola put the great department store of The Ladies' Paradise, the one that swallows up every little shop around it, on the corner of this street and Rue Neuve-Saint-Augustin; the novel opens with Denise, just arrived from the provinces, stopped dead by its windows. Zola spent months in the Bon Marché researching it. The store is invented, but walk a few minutes north and the Galeries Lafayette and Printemps, the real shopping palaces of the nineteenth century, are still open for business
note: 左拉把《妇女乐园》里那家吞掉周围小店的大百货公司放在米肖迪埃尔街和新圣奥古斯丁街的转角，小说开头，外省姑娘德妮丝一到巴黎就被它的橱窗看呆了。左拉为写这本书在乐蓬马歇百货里泡了好几个月。百货店是虚构的，但往北走几分钟就是老佛爷和春天百货，19 世纪的购物天堂至今还在营业

name: Place du Carrousel, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 卡鲁塞尔广场
note_en: This is the setting of Baudelaire's 'The Swan'. When Haussmann rebuilt Paris, a whole old quarter wedged between the wings of the Louvre was torn down, and the poet, crossing the new Place du Carrousel, remembers a swan he once saw here, escaped from its cage and flapping in a dry gutter, and writes that the shape of a city changes faster than the human heart. He dedicated the poem to Victor Hugo, then in exile. Today the Arc du Carrousel stands at one end and I. M. Pei's glass pyramid at the other
note: 波德莱尔的《天鹅》写的就是这里：豪斯曼改造巴黎时，夹在卢浮宫两翼之间的一片旧街区被拆光，诗人走过新修的卡鲁塞尔广场，想起当年在这里看见一只逃出笼子的天鹅在干涸的街沟里扑腾，写下“城市的模样变得比人心还快”。诗是献给流亡中的雨果的。今天广场一头是卡鲁塞尔凯旋门，一头是贝聿铭的玻璃金字塔

name: Luxembourg Gardens, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 卢森堡公园
note_en: In Les Misérables Marius walks in the Luxembourg Garden every day, and at the end of a quiet path he notices an old white-haired man and his daughter, Jean Valjean and Cosette. A year later Cosette has grown into a beautiful young woman, they exchange one look under the chestnut trees, and Marius falls in love. You can drag the park's green metal chairs into any patch of shade you like; the Medici Fountain is the quietest corner
note: 《悲惨世界》里马吕斯天天来卢森堡公园散步，在一条僻静的小径尽头注意到一位白发老人和他的女儿——就是冉阿让和珂赛特。一年后再见，珂赛特已经长成美丽的少女，两人在栗树下交换了一个眼神，马吕斯就此坠入爱河。公园里的绿色铁椅可以随便搬到树荫下坐，美第奇喷泉一带最安静

name: Old Port, Marseille
name_zh: 马赛 · 老港
note_en: The Count of Monte Cristo opens on 24 February 1815, as the three-master Pharaon sails into the Old Port of Marseille, with crowds packed onto Fort Saint-Jean at the harbor mouth to watch her come in and nineteen-year-old Edmond Dantès, her first mate, standing at the bow with everything ahead of him; within days he is arrested at his own engagement feast. The Old Port is still the heart of Marseille, fishermen sell the morning's catch on the quay every day, and the new MuCEM museum stands right next to Fort Saint-Jean
note: 《基督山伯爵》开头，1815 年 2 月 24 日，三桅船“法老号”驶进马赛老港，港口入口处圣让堡上挤满了看热闹的人，十九岁的大副唐泰斯站在船头，前途一片光明——几天后他就在订婚宴上被捕。老港至今是马赛的中心，每天早上码头边都有渔民摆摊卖刚上岸的鱼，圣让堡旁边就是新建的欧洲与地中海文明博物馆

name: Château d’If, Marseille
name_zh: 马赛 · 伊夫堡
note_en: Framed and thrown into this island fortress, Dantès spends fourteen years here; in the dungeons he meets the Abbé Faria, tunneling his way out, who educates him and tells him of the treasure of Monte Cristo, and in the end Dantès escapes by taking the dead abbé's place in his shroud and being thrown into the sea. The novel is so famous that the castle has labeled one cell as Dantès's and another as Faria's, with a hole knocked between them. Boats leave from the Old Port, twenty minutes away
note: 唐泰斯被诬陷后关进这座海上石堡，一关就是十四年，在地牢里遇见了挖地道的法利亚长老，学到学问，也得知基督山岛的宝藏；最后他钻进长老的裹尸袋，被当作尸体扔进大海逃了出来。小说太出名，堡里干脆给“唐泰斯的牢房”和“法利亚长老的牢房”挂了牌，中间还凿了个洞。从老港坐船二十分钟就到

name: Alphonse Daudet’s Mill, Fontvieille
name_zh: 方特维耶 · 都德磨坊
note_en: Letters from My Windmill opens with the narrator telling us he has bought a ruined windmill in Provence, and from it he writes to his friends in Paris, telling the tales of Father Gaucher's elixir and Monsieur Seguin's goat. In truth Daudet wrote most of it in Paris, though he often stayed with cousins at the nearby Château de Montauban. This Saint-Pierre mill on the hill above Fontvieille has become 'Daudet's mill' for readers ever since, with a small Daudet museum inside and pine woods and the Alpilles all around
note: 《磨坊书简》开篇，叙述者说他在普罗旺斯买下了一座荒废的风车磨坊，在里面给巴黎的朋友写信，讲高谢神父的药酒、塞甘先生的山羊这些故事。其实都德大多是在巴黎写的，只是常来附近表亲的蒙托邦城堡小住。方特维耶山坡上这座圣皮埃尔磨坊就成了读者心中的“都德磨坊”，里面有一个小小的都德纪念馆，周围是松林和阿尔皮耶山的景色

name: Alsace — setting of The Last Lesson
name_zh: 阿尔萨斯 · 《最后一课》的故事地域
note_en: Daudet's 'The Last Lesson' is set in an unnamed Alsatian village. After the Franco-Prussian War of 1871, Alsace was handed to Germany and Berlin ordered the schools to teach only German; little Franz, late for school, learns that this is Monsieur Hamel's last French lesson, and at the end the teacher writes 'Vive la France!' on the blackboard. Alsace returned to France only in 1918, and the villages along its Wine Route still speak both French and Alsatian
note: 都德的《最后一课》发生在阿尔萨斯一个没有点名的村子：1871 年普法战争后阿尔萨斯割给德国，柏林下令学校只准教德语，小弗朗茨迟到走进教室，才知道这是韩麦尔先生上的最后一堂法语课，下课时老师在黑板上写下“法兰西万岁！”。阿尔萨斯直到 1918 年才回到法国，今天沿葡萄酒之路的村庄还说着法语和阿尔萨斯方言
coord_checked: Alsace — setting of The Last Lesson — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsace

name: Maison de Jules Verne, Amiens
name_zh: 亚眠 · 凡尔纳故居
note_en: Jules Verne lived in this house with a tower in Amiens from 1882 to 1900, and it was here that he wrote Robur the Conqueror (1886), with its flying machine the Albatross. He sat on the Amiens town council for years and is buried in the city. The house is now a museum, packed from cellar to attic with his manuscripts, maps, model ships and early illustrated editions, and his study is at the top of the tower
note: 凡尔纳 1882 到 1900 年住在亚眠这座带塔楼的房子里，《征服者罗比尔》（1886）里那艘能在空中飞的“信天翁号”就是在这段时间写出来的。他在亚眠当了多年市议员，最后也葬在这里。故居现在是博物馆，从地下室到阁楼摆满了他的手稿、地图、船模和早期版本的插图书，塔楼顶上就是他的书房

name: Villa La Guillette, Étretat
name_zh: 埃特雷塔 · 莫泊桑吉耶特别墅
note_en: Maupassant grew up in Étretat on the Normandy coast, and once he was famous he built himself a villa here, La Guillette, where he spent his summers writing. His well-known essay on the novel that opens Pierre and Jean is signed 'La Guillette, Étretat, September 1887', while the novel itself takes place in Le Havre, a few dozen kilometers away. The villa still stands, a few minutes' walk from the white cliffs Monet painted again and again
note: 莫泊桑在诺曼底海边的埃特雷塔长大，成名后在这里盖了自己的别墅“吉耶特”，夏天就在这里写作。《皮埃尔与让》卷首那篇著名的小说论《论小说》，结尾就署着“吉耶特别墅，埃特雷塔，1887 年 9 月”，小说本身则发生在几十公里外的勒阿弗尔。别墅还在，离莫奈画过无数次的白色悬崖只有几分钟路

name: Grand Hôtel, Cabourg
name_zh: 卡堡 · 大饭店
prototype_of: 《追忆似水年华》里巴尔贝克海滨大旅馆的原型：1907 到 1914 年，普鲁斯特几乎每个夏天都住在卡堡的这家大饭店，在小说里把它变成了巴尔贝克，叙述者第一次看见阿尔贝蒂娜和那群“少女”就在这里的海堤上。他写夜里灯火通明的餐厅像一只巨大的水族箱，镇上的穷人贴着玻璃往里看。饭店至今照常营业，门前的海滨步道就叫马塞尔·普鲁斯特步道
prototype_of_en: The model for the Grand Hotel at Balbec in In Search of Lost Time. Proust spent nearly every summer from 1907 to 1914 at this hotel in Cabourg and turned it into Balbec; it's on the promenade here that the narrator first sees Albertine and her band of girls. He describes the lit-up dining room at night as a vast aquarium, with the town's poor pressing against the glass to look in. The hotel is still open, and the seafront promenade outside is named after Marcel Proust

name: Palais Garnier, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 加尼叶歌剧院
note: 勒鲁的《歌剧魅影》就发生在这座金碧辉煌的歌剧院里：戴面具的埃里克藏身在地下深处，爱上了年轻的歌手克里斯汀。小说里最神秘的地下湖并非凭空捏造——建造时挖到了地下水，建筑师加尼叶干脆修了一个巨大的蓄水池托住地基，至今还在，消防员在里面潜水训练。大厅、大楼梯和夏加尔画的穹顶都可以参观，5 号包厢门上还挂着“魅影专用”的牌子
note_en: Leroux's The Phantom of the Opera is set in this gilded opera house, where the masked Erik hides deep underground and falls in love with the young singer Christine. The novel's eerie underground lake wasn't pure invention: the builders struck groundwater, so Charles Garnier built a huge water tank to carry the foundations, and it's still there today, used by firefighters for diving practice. You can tour the foyers, the grand staircase and the auditorium with its Chagall ceiling, and Box 5 still has a plaque saying it belongs to the Phantom

name: Aiguille and Porte d'Aval, Étretat
name_zh: 埃特雷塔 · 空心岩柱与阿瓦勒门
note: 莫里斯·勒布朗在《空心岩柱》里让怪盗亚森·罗宾把宝藏藏进埃特雷塔海边这根七十米高的白垩岩柱，少年侦探博特雷在黄昏时看见一缕青烟从岩柱顶端的缝里冒出来，才明白它是空心的。勒布朗在镇上住了几十年，他的别墅“亚森·罗宾庄园”现在是博物馆。沿着悬崖步道走到阿瓦勒门上方，岩柱和天然石拱就在眼前
note_en: In The Hollow Needle, Maurice Leblanc has the gentleman thief Arsène Lupin hide his treasure inside this seventy-meter chalk stack off the beach at Étretat; the boy detective Beautrelet realizes it is hollow when he sees a thread of smoke rising from a crack near the top at dusk. Leblanc lived in the town for decades, and his villa, the Clos Arsène Lupin, is now a museum. Walk the cliff path up over the Porte d'Aval and the needle and the natural arch are right in front of you

name: Meung-sur-Loire
name_zh: 卢瓦尔河畔默恩
note: 《三个火枪手》开篇，1625 年 4 月的第一个星期一，十八岁的达达尼昂骑着一匹黄色的老马走进这座卢瓦尔河边的小镇，就在客栈门口和一位陌生贵族起了冲突——那就是红衣主教的心腹罗什福尔，整部小说的恩怨由此开始。大仲马还特意提到这里是《玫瑰传奇》作者的故乡。镇上的城堡和老街都在，离奥尔良只有半小时车程
note_en: The Three Musketeers opens here, on the first Monday of April 1625, when eighteen-year-old d'Artagnan rides into this little Loire town on an old yellow horse and picks a quarrel at the inn door with a stranger who turns out to be Rochefort, the Cardinal's agent, starting the feud that runs through the whole novel. Dumas makes a point of noting that the author of the Romance of the Rose was born here. The château and the old streets are still there, half an hour from Orléans

name: Place Edmond-Rostand (old Place Saint-Michel), Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 老圣米歇尔广场（缪尚咖啡馆）
note: 《悲惨世界》里安灼拉、古费拉克和 ABC 朋友会的大学生们，就在“先贤祠附近、圣米歇尔广场上的缪尚咖啡馆”后厅里密谋共和，马吕斯也是在这里被拉进了他们的圈子。咖啡馆是虚构的，雨果写书时那座圣米歇尔广场在卢森堡公园门口，就是今天的埃德蒙-罗斯丹广场，不是塞纳河边后来修的那座喷泉广场。站在这里，一边是卢森堡公园，一边沿苏夫洛街望得见先贤祠
note_en: In Les Misérables, Enjolras, Courfeyrac and the students of the Friends of the ABC plot their republic in the back room of the Café Musain, 'a little café near the Pantheon' on the Place Saint-Michel, and it's here that Marius is drawn into their circle. The café is invented, and the Place Saint-Michel of Hugo's day stood at the gate of the Luxembourg Garden, where Place Edmond-Rostand is now, not the fountain square by the Seine that was built later. Stand here with the Luxembourg on one side and look down rue Soufflot to the Panthéon

name: Rue Mondétour and Rue Rambuteau (Corinthe and the barricade), Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 蒙代图尔街（科林斯酒馆与街垒）
note: 1832 年 6 月起义，ABC 朋友会在麻厂街的科林斯酒馆门前筑起街垒，安灼拉、伽弗洛什和朋友们几乎全都死在这里，冉阿让背着昏迷的马吕斯从这里钻进下水道。雨果写书时，这片中世纪的窄巷已经被朗布托街拆平，他在小说里特意告诉读者：如今走进朗布托街，对面就是蒙代图尔街，当年的酒馆和街垒就在这里。蒙代图尔街还在，就在中央市场东北角，现在两旁都是咖啡馆
note_en: During the uprising of June 1832, the Friends of the ABC built their barricade outside the Corinthe tavern on the Rue de la Chanvrerie; Enjolras, Gavroche and nearly all their friends died here, and Jean Valjean carried the unconscious Marius down into the sewers from this spot. By the time Hugo wrote the novel, these medieval alleys had been flattened to make the Rue Rambuteau, and he tells his readers exactly where to look: enter the Rue Rambuteau, and the tavern and the barricade stood opposite the Rue Mondétour. Rue Mondétour is still there, at the northeast corner of Les Halles, lined with cafés
coord_checked: Base Adresse Nationale, 102 rue Rambuteau; site identified by Commission du Vieux Paris, 19 October 2017, pp. 33–35 — https://api-adresse.data.gouv.fr/search/?q=102%20rue%20Rambuteau%2075001%20Paris&limit=1

name: Musée des Égouts de Paris
name_zh: 巴黎下水道博物馆
note: 《悲惨世界》第五部，冉阿让背着受伤的马吕斯穿过巴黎的下水道逃出生天，雨果为此专门写了整整一卷下水道的历史，说“巴黎的下面还有一个巴黎”。小说里的路线从麻厂街一直走到塞纳河边的出口。今天在阿尔玛桥边可以真的走进一段下水道，看看那些标着地面街名的地下隧道
note_en: In Part Five of Les Misérables, Jean Valjean escapes through the sewers of Paris with the wounded Marius on his back, and Hugo devotes a whole book to the history of the sewers, writing that 'Paris has beneath it another Paris'. In the novel the route runs from the Rue de la Chanvrerie all the way to an outlet on the Seine. Today, by the Pont de l'Alma, you can walk into a working stretch of the sewers, where the tunnels carry the names of the streets above

name: Église Saint-Sulpice, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 圣叙尔皮斯教堂
note: 《达·芬奇密码》让这座教堂一夜成名：小说里，白化病修士塞拉斯半夜来到这里，以为地上那条黄铜线是巴黎的“玫瑰线”，砸开方尖碑下的地板寻找拱心石。其实这是 18 世纪的天文日晷，用来测定春分和复活节的日期。来的游客多到教堂专门立了告示牌，说明这条铜线和小说说的毫无关系。教堂里还有德拉克洛瓦的壁画
note_en: The Da Vinci Code made this church famous overnight. In the novel, the albino monk Silas comes here at night, takes the brass line set into the floor for the Paris 'Rose Line', and smashes the paving at the foot of the obelisk looking for the keystone. In fact it's an eighteenth-century astronomical gnomon, built to fix the date of the spring equinox and Easter, and so many visitors came that the church put up a notice explaining the line has nothing to do with the novel. Don't miss the Delacroix murals inside

name: Fontaine des Innocents, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 无辜者喷泉
note: 《香水》的主人公格雷诺耶 1738 年 7 月就出生在这里：那时这是无辜者公墓，紧挨着铁器街的鱼市，聚斯金德说这是“全法国最臭的地方”，他的母亲在鱼摊下生下他，转身就想把他和鱼内脏一起扔掉。公墓在 18 世纪末被清空，骨头搬进了地下墓穴，只有这座文艺复兴时期的喷泉留下来，被移到了广场中央
note_en: Grenouille, the hero of Perfume, is born here in July 1738, when this was the Cemetery of the Innocents, next to the fish market on the Rue aux Fers; Süskind calls it the most putrid spot in all France, and his mother gives birth under her fish stall and tries to leave him with the fish guts. The cemetery was cleared at the end of the eighteenth century and the bones moved to the Catacombs; only this Renaissance fountain survived, moved to the middle of the square

name: Shakespeare and Company, Paris
name_zh: 巴黎 · 莎士比亚书店
note: 海明威在《流动的盛宴》里回忆 20 年代的巴黎，那时他穷得买不起书，西尔维娅·比奇的莎士比亚书店让他想借多少就借多少，乔伊斯的《尤利西斯》也是她出版的。原来的书店在奥德翁街，1941 年关门；今天塞纳河边、正对圣母院的这家是乔治·惠特曼 1951 年开的，后来沿用了这个名字，楼上还让年轻作家免费借宿
note_en: In A Moveable Feast, Hemingway remembers the Paris of the 1920s, when he was too poor to buy books and Sylvia Beach let him borrow as many as he liked from Shakespeare and Company; she was also the publisher of Joyce's Ulysses. Her shop on Rue de l'Odéon closed in 1941. The one you visit today, on the Seine opposite Notre-Dame, was opened by George Whitman in 1951 and later took the name, and young writers can still sleep among the books upstairs

name: Saint-Exupéry statue, Place Bellecour, Lyon
name_zh: 里昂贝勒库尔广场 · 圣埃克苏佩里与小王子像
note: 《小王子》的作者圣埃克苏佩里 1900 年出生在里昂，离贝勒库尔广场只有几条街。广场西边立着一根白色石柱，上面坐着这位飞行员作家，小王子站在他身后——这是全世界读者来里昂必拍的地方。他 1944 年驾机执行侦察任务时在地中海上空失踪，里昂的机场也以他命名
note_en: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, author of The Little Prince, was born in Lyon in 1900, a few streets from Place Bellecour. On the square stands a white column with the pilot-writer sitting on top and the Little Prince standing behind him, and readers from all over the world come to photograph it. He vanished over the Mediterranean on a reconnaissance flight in 1944, and Lyon's airport is named after him

name: Ménerbes
name_zh: 梅纳村
note: 英国广告人彼得·梅尔 1987 年和妻子在吕贝隆山区这座小村旁买下一座老农舍，把第一年的生活一个月一个月写成了《普罗旺斯的一年》：一月的密斯特拉尔风、永远修不完的房子、松露、本地人的饭桌。这本书成了全球畅销书，也让成群的读者涌进这个原本安静的村子。村子建在山脊上，俯瞰着葡萄园和樱桃园
note_en: In 1987 the English advertising man Peter Mayle and his wife bought an old farmhouse outside this hill village in the Luberon, and he wrote up their first year month by month in A Year in Provence: the January mistral, the builders who never finished, truffles, long lunches with the neighbors. It became a worldwide bestseller and sent crowds of readers to a village that had been very quiet. Ménerbes sits on a ridge above the vineyards and cherry orchards
